name: Walkman
blurb: Sony's pocket cassette player with headphones, launched in 1979
title: Sony Walkman: When It Came Out, Price and What Happened
description: The Walkman was Sony's portable cassette player, launched in Japan on 1 July 1979. Cassette models ended in Japan in 2010; the name lives on in digital players.
answer: The Walkman was a pocket-sized cassette player with lightweight headphones that let you carry your music with you, launched by Sony in Japan on 1 July 1979 as the TPS-L2. It turned "personal stereo" into an everyday habit, and Sony sold more than 220 million cassette Walkmans before ending production in Japan in 2010. Sony still uses the Walkman name for its digital music players.

body: A cassette Walkman was only a little bigger than the tape inside it: a flip-open door, a row of buttons for play, fast-forward, rewind and stop, a headphone socket and a few AA or AAA batteries. Later models added auto-reverse, so the player switched to side B on its own instead of you flipping the tape; Sony's first Walkman with auto-reverse and Dolby noise reduction came in 1982.

The original TPS-L2 could only play, not record, and many retailers doubted anyone would want a tape machine without a record button. It sold about 30,000 units in its first two months and around 50 million within a decade, according to AFP.

body: Listening moved to digital. CD players, then MiniDisc and MP3 players, and above all Apple's iPod, took over the job. When Sony announced the end of the cassette Walkman in Japan in 2010, its spokeswoman said customers' listening habits had shifted to digital audio and demand for cassette models had fallen.

Not a new cassette Walkman from Sony; those are now second-hand and collector items. The brand itself is alive: Sony still sells digital music players under the Walkman name, such as the A and ZX series. With the small cassette revival of recent years, other companies have also put out new portable tape players.

ul: "Walkman" became the generic word for any portable tape player, whatever the brand.
Auto-reverse models saved you from opening the door to flip the tape.
Batteries ran down and the music slowed and dragged before it stopped.
Taping songs off the radio and then listening to them on the bus.

faq.q: How much did the first Walkman cost?
faq.a: The TPS-L2 sold for about ¥33,000 in Japan in 1979, roughly $150 at the time.

faq.q: When did Sony stop making cassette Walkmans?
faq.a: Production in Japan ended in 2010, with the announcement made that October after a final batch shipped to stores.
Yes, but only digital music players. The cassette models are discontinued.
